books.title: Ganita Prakash: Textbook of Mathematics for Grade 6
books.edition: Reprint 2026-27 (First Edition August 2024; reprinted December 2024 and January 2026)

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings

topics.title: What is Mathematics?
objectives: Student can describe mathematics as the search for patterns and for explanations of why those patterns exist
Student can give examples of how mathematics helps in everyday life
visualIdeas: patterns in nature, buildings and numbers arranged as a collage

topics.title: Patterns in Numbers
objectives: Student can recognise and extend number sequences: counting, odd, even, triangular, square and cube numbers, Virahanka numbers and powers of 2
Student can describe the rule behind each sequence in words
visualIdeas: a table of number sequences with the next few terms left blank

topics.title: Visualising Number Sequences
objectives: Student can draw dot pictures that show why triangular, square and cube numbers get their names
Student can use a picture to predict the next term of a sequence
visualIdeas: dot triangles, dot squares and stacked cubes growing step by step

topics.title: Relations among Number Sequences
objectives: Student can show that adding consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 gives square numbers
Student can explain such a relation using a picture rather than only calculation
visualIdeas: an L-shaped layer of dots added to a square to make the next square

topics.title: Patterns in Shapes
objectives: Student can recognise and extend shape sequences: regular polygons, complete graphs, stacked squares, stacked triangles and Koch snowflake iterations
Student can describe the rule that takes each shape in a sequence to the next one
visualIdeas: regular polygons from triangle upward in a row
first steps of the Koch snowflake

topics.title: Relation to Number Sequences
objectives: Student can relate a shape sequence to a number sequence, such as the sides of regular polygons to the counting numbers from 3
Student can count the parts of shapes in a sequence (sides, lines, small squares or triangles) and name the number sequence they form
visualIdeas: complete graphs with their line counts written underneath

topics.title: Point
objectives: Student can explain that a point determines a location and is named by a capital letter
Student can mark and label points on paper and identify points in everyday objects such as the tip of a compass
visualIdeas: a map with places marked as labelled points

topics.title: Line Segment
objectives: Student can explain that a line segment is the shortest path between two points and name it by its end points
Student can draw and measure line segments
visualIdeas: two points joined by a straight path and by a curved path for comparison

topics.title: Line
objectives: Student can explain that a line is a line segment extended indefinitely in both directions
Student can find how many lines pass through one point and through two given points
visualIdeas: a line segment with arrows extending at both ends

topics.title: Ray
objectives: Student can explain that a ray starts at a point and goes on indefinitely in one direction, and name it correctly
Student can distinguish between a line segment, a line and a ray
visualIdeas: a torch beam drawn as a ray from its starting point

topics.title: Angle
objectives: Student can describe an angle as two rays starting from a common point, and name its vertex and arms
Student can name an angle using three letters with the vertex in the middle
visualIdeas: two rays OP and OM forming angle POM with vertex and arms labelled

topics.title: Comparing Angles
objectives: Student can compare two angles by placing one over the other
Student can explain that the size of an angle is the amount of turn about the vertex, not the length of its arms
visualIdeas: two angles with long and short arms superimposed to compare openings

topics.title: Making Rotating Arms
objectives: Student can make rotating arms with paper straws and a clip and show angles of different sizes
Student can arrange angles from smallest to largest by comparing them
visualIdeas: two straws joined by a clip opening through different angles

topics.title: Special Types of Angles
objectives: Student can identify a straight angle as a half turn and a right angle as a quarter turn
Student can recognise perpendicular lines as lines that meet at a right angle
visualIdeas: a book cover opened through a half turn and a quarter turn

topics.title: Measuring Angles
objectives: Student can explain that one full turn is 360 degrees and use this to find degree measures of other turns
Student can measure an angle using a protractor
visualIdeas: a protractor placed on an angle with the baseline and vertex aligned

topics.title: Drawing Angles
objectives: Student can draw an angle of a given measure using a ruler and a protractor
Student can place the protractor centre on the vertex and align the base arm with the 0 line before marking the turn
visualIdeas: steps to draw a 30 degree angle TIN with a protractor

topics.title: Types of Angles and their Measures
objectives: Student can classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex from their measures
Student can estimate whether an angle is acute, obtuse or reflex before measuring it
visualIdeas: a fan of angles labelled acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex with degree ranges

topics.title: Numbers can Tell us Things
objectives: Student can work out what a number says when children call out how many taller neighbours they have
Student can reason about which arrangements of children are possible or impossible
visualIdeas: a line of children of different heights each holding up a number

topics.title: Supercells
objectives: Student can identify a supercell as a cell whose number is larger than its adjacent cells
Student can fill a table so that it has a required number of supercells and explain why
visualIdeas: a number grid with supercells coloured

topics.title: Patterns of Numbers on the Number Line
objectives: Student can place large numbers at their approximate positions on a number line
Student can identify the numbers marked on a number line and pick the smallest and largest in a sequence
visualIdeas: a number line from 1000 to 10000 with numbers placed on it

topics.title: Playing with Digits
objectives: Student can count how many numbers have one, two, three, four and five digits
Student can find digit sums and look for numbers with a given digit sum
visualIdeas: a table of 1-digit to 5-digit number ranges with counts

topics.title: Pretty Palindromic Patterns
objectives: Student can identify palindromic numbers
Student can use the reverse-and-add process to reach a palindrome
visualIdeas: a reverse-and-add chain ending in a palindrome

topics.title: The Magic Number of Kaprekar
objectives: Student can carry out Kaprekar's routine on a 4-digit number, subtracting the smallest arrangement of its digits from the largest, and observe that it reaches 6174
Student can state that D.R. Kaprekar, a school teacher from Devlali, discovered this pattern in 1949
visualIdeas: a chain of Kaprekar steps converging on 6174

topics.title: Clock and Calendar Numbers
objectives: Student can find all times of a given pattern, such as 4:44 or 12:21, on a 12-hour clock
Student can find dates with digit patterns, such as palindromic dates, and reason about when a calendar can be reused
visualIdeas: a digital clock showing a palindromic time like 12:21

topics.title: Mental Math
objectives: Student can make target numbers by adding and subtracting given numbers mentally
Student can use number combinations to calculate sums and differences quickly
visualIdeas: number cards combined to hit a target number

topics.title: Playing with Number Patterns
objectives: Student can find the sum of numbers arranged in a pattern using a quicker method than adding one by one
Student can share and compare different methods of finding the same sum
visualIdeas: a dot arrangement grouped into equal rows for quick adding

topics.title: An Unsolved Mystery — the Collatz Conjecture!
objectives: Student can generate a Collatz sequence by halving even numbers and applying 3n + 1 to odd numbers
Student can explain that it is still unknown whether every starting number reaches 1
visualIdeas: a branching diagram of Collatz sequences ending at 1

topics.title: Simple Estimation
objectives: Student can make reasonable estimates of large quantities from everyday life
Student can explain how they arrived at an estimate
visualIdeas: an estimation card asking how many students are in the school

topics.title: Games and Winning Strategies
objectives: Student can play the game of 21 and discover a strategy that guarantees a win
Student can explain why the winning strategy works
visualIdeas: a game board counting up to 21 with winning numbers highlighted

topics.title: Collecting and Organising Data
objectives: Student can collect data and organise it in a table using tally marks
Student can find frequencies and answer questions from a frequency table
visualIdeas: a tally table of favourite fruits in a class

topics.title: Pictographs
objectives: Student can read a pictograph in which one picture may stand for more than one item
Student can draw a pictograph with a stated scale
visualIdeas: a pictograph of books read with one symbol standing for 5 books

topics.title: Bar Graphs
objectives: Student can read and interpret bar graphs with a stated scale
Student can draw conclusions from a bar graph
visualIdeas: a vertical bar graph of students' modes of travel to school

topics.title: Drawing a Bar Graph
objectives: Student can choose a suitable scale and draw a bar graph with bars of uniform width
Student can label axes and title a bar graph
visualIdeas: steps to draw a bar graph with gridlines and scale chosen

topics.title: Artistic and Aesthetic Considerations
objectives: Student can explain how colour, pictures and bar direction affect how clearly a graph conveys data
Student can recognise when a fancy graph is misleading
visualIdeas: two graphs of the same data, one clear and one misleading

topics.title: Common Multiples and Common Factors
objectives: Student can find common multiples of two numbers through games like Idli-Vada
Student can find common factors of two numbers
visualIdeas: a number line with jumps of two sizes landing on common multiples

topics.title: Prime Numbers
objectives: Student can define prime and composite numbers by their number of factors
Student can use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to find primes up to 100
visualIdeas: a 1-to-100 grid with multiples crossed out leaving the primes

topics.title: Co-prime Numbers for Safekeeping Treasures
objectives: Student can identify co-prime pairs as numbers with no common factor other than 1
Student can check whether a pair of numbers is co-prime
visualIdeas: a treasure game where two numbers cannot both be reached by one jump size

topics.title: Prime Factorisation
objectives: Student can express a number as a product of prime factors
Student can use prime factorisations to check whether two numbers are co-prime, and explain why a single factor pair is not enough
visualIdeas: a factor tree splitting a number into primes

topics.title: Divisibility Tests
objectives: Student can use divisibility tests for 10, 5, 2, 4 and 8
Student can explain why the tests for 4 and 8 depend only on the last two or three digits
visualIdeas: a number with its last digits highlighted for each test

topics.title: Fun with Numbers
objectives: Student can explain what makes a number special in different ways, such as being prime or a square
Student can solve puzzles involving primes
visualIdeas: a box of numbers with reasons each could be special

topics.title: Perimeter
objectives: Student can define the perimeter of a polygon as the sum of the lengths of its sides
Student can find the perimeter of a rectangle as twice the sum of length and width and of a square as four times its side
Student can solve problems involving perimeter, such as finding a missing side
visualIdeas: a rectangle with its sides being walked around and added

topics.title: Area
objectives: Student can define area as the measure of the region enclosed by a closed figure, in square units
Student can find areas of rectangles and squares and estimate areas of irregular shapes on squared paper
Student can show that two figures can have the same area with different perimeters, or the same perimeter with different areas
visualIdeas: a shape on squared grid paper with full and half squares counted
two rectangles with equal area but different perimeters

topics.title: Area of a Triangle
objectives: Student can show by cutting a rectangle along a diagonal that each triangle is half the rectangle's area
Student can find areas of triangles on squared paper by fitting them into rectangles
visualIdeas: a rectangle cut along its diagonal into two matching triangles

topics.title: Fractional Units and Equal Shares
objectives: Student can share a whole equally and name each share as a fractional unit such as one-half or one-third
Student can explain why 1/9 is smaller than 1/5 by thinking of a roti shared among more children
visualIdeas: a roti divided into equal shares among children

topics.title: Fractional Units as Parts of a Whole
objectives: Student can identify the fractional unit for a part of a whole and write fractions like 3/4 as three one-fourths
Student can measure a piece of a whole, such as a piece of chikki, using a suitable fractional unit
visualIdeas: a rectangle divided into equal parts with some shaded

topics.title: Measuring Using Fractional Units
objectives: Student can fold a paper strip into equal parts and measure lengths in fractional units
Student can express the length of each part of a folded unit strip as a fraction of one unit
visualIdeas: a paper strip folded into halves, quarters and eighths

topics.title: Marking Fraction Lengths on the Number Line
objectives: Student can mark fractions on a number line by dividing a unit into equal parts
Student can read the length of a line on a number line as a fraction, including lengths more than one unit
visualIdeas: a number line from 0 to 2 with quarters marked

topics.title: Mixed Fractions
objectives: Student can tell fractions less than 1 from fractions greater than 1 by comparing numerator and denominator
Student can convert between fractions greater than 1 and mixed fractions
visualIdeas: 7/4 shown as one whole and three quarters

topics.title: Equivalent Fractions
objectives: Student can find equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same number
Student can write a fraction in its lowest terms
visualIdeas: fraction strips showing 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 aligned

topics.title: Comparing Fractions
objectives: Student can compare fractions with the same denominator or the same numerator
Student can compare fractions with different denominators by converting them to equivalent fractions with a common denominator
visualIdeas: 4/5 and 7/9 both rewritten over 45 for comparison

topics.title: Addition and Subtraction of Fractions
objectives: Student can add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
Student can add and subtract fractions with different denominators using equivalent fractions
visualIdeas: fraction strips placed end to end to show a sum

topics.title: A Pinch of History
objectives: Student can state that a fraction was called bhinna in ancient India
Student can explain that the way we write fractions today originated in India, as seen in the Bakshali manuscript, and that the bar between numerator and denominator was added later by Al-Hassar
visualIdeas: the Bakshali-manuscript way of writing one-half beside the modern form

topics.title: Artwork
objectives: Student can use a compass to draw circles and explain that all points of a circle are at the same distance (the radius) from its centre
Student can construct wave patterns from half circles drawn on a line
visualIdeas: a compass drawing a circle with the radius marked
a wave made of alternating half circles

topics.title: Squares and Rectangles
objectives: Student can state the properties of rectangles and squares: opposite sides equal and all angles right angles, with all sides equal for a square
Student can name a rectangle correctly by going around its vertices in order
visualIdeas: a rectangle PQRS with equal opposite sides and right angles marked

topics.title: Constructing Squares and Rectangles
objectives: Student can construct a rectangle or square of given side lengths using a ruler, compass and protractor
Student can draw a rough diagram first to plan a construction
visualIdeas: construction steps for a 5 cm by 3 cm rectangle

topics.title: An Exploration in Rectangles
objectives: Student can predict where points moving along two sides of a rectangle will be closest and farthest, then check by measuring
Student can construct a rectangle of given sides and place points on its sides to meet a given condition
visualIdeas: a rectangle with points X and Y sliding along two sides

topics.title: Exploring Diagonals of Rectangles and Squares
objectives: Student can show by construction and measurement that the diagonals of a rectangle are equal
Student can construct a rectangle given one side and a diagonal
visualIdeas: a rectangle with both diagonals drawn and the angles they make marked

topics.title: Points Equidistant from Two Given Points
objectives: Student can use intersecting arcs to find a point at a given distance from two given points
Student can plan and construct a figure such as a house shape from given lengths
visualIdeas: two arcs from two points meeting at a point
the house figure with all border lines of 5 cm

topics.title: Line of Symmetry
objectives: Student can identify lines of symmetry in figures by folding or reflecting
Student can complete a figure given half of it and its line of symmetry
Student can recognise that a figure may have several lines of symmetry or none
visualIdeas: a butterfly, a rangoli and a pinwheel with their lines of symmetry drawn

topics.title: Rotational Symmetry
objectives: Student can identify the angles of symmetry and centre of rotation of a figure
Student can decide whether a figure has rotational symmetry, line symmetry, both or neither
visualIdeas: a pinwheel rotated in steps about its centre with angles marked

topics.title: Bela's Building of Fun
objectives: Student can use floors above and below ground in a building to represent positive and negative numbers
Student can read and write integers and place them on a number line
Student can interpret addition as starting position plus movement and subtraction as target minus starting position
visualIdeas: a building with lift buttons from -3 to +5 drawn as a vertical number line

topics.title: The Token Model
objectives: Student can use positive and negative tokens, with zero pairs, to add integers
Student can use tokens to subtract integers, adding zero pairs when needed
visualIdeas: positive and negative tokens with zero pairs cancelling

topics.title: Integers in Other Places
objectives: Student can use integers for credits and debits in a bank account
Student can represent heights above and below sea level in a geographical cross section and temperatures below zero using integers
visualIdeas: a bank passbook page with deposits and withdrawals as signed numbers
a geographical cross section with sea level marked as 0 m

topics.title: Explorations with Integers
objectives: Student can complete integer grids whose rows and columns add up to a given sum
Student can find patterns in integer grids, such as rows and columns that add up to zero
visualIdeas: a hollow integer grid with rows and columns summing to zero

topics.title: A Pinch of History
objectives: Student can state that integers including zero and negative numbers were first conceived and used in Asia
Student can apply Brahmagupta's rules for adding and subtracting positive numbers, negative numbers and zero
visualIdeas: Brahmagupta's rules for addition written beside number-line examples
